title: SWPC CME Discussion: Halo CME Arriving 16 Mar

fields.title: *** EXERCISE EXERCISE EXERCISE *** Forecast Discussion, CME analysis: fast halo CME from the X2.1 flare expected to arrive 16 March

arrival.expectedLevel: G3 (Strong) likely after arrival, with a chance of G4 (Severe)

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The fast halo CME associated with the X2.1 flare (peak 2027 Mar 15 2331 UTC) is expected to arrive at Earth between 16 Mar 1600 UTC and 16 Mar 2200 UTC. The arrival window is uncertain by several hours. G3 (Strong) levels are likely after arrival, with a chance of G4 (Severe). The WATA50 G3 Geomagnetic Storm Watch for 16 Mar remains in effect.

sections.heading: Solar Activity and CME Analysis
sections.text: The X2.1 flare came from a magnetically complex region near disk center and caused an R3 (Strong) radio blackout on the sunlit side, which has ended. Coronagraph imagery shows a full halo CME first visible at 15/2348 UTC, with a plane-of-sky speed estimated near 2,100 km/s. Model runs with this input bring the leading edge to Earth about 16 to 22 hours after launch.

sections.heading: Arrival Estimate
sections.text: The model's central arrival time is 16 Mar 1900 UTC, with an uncertainty of about plus or minus 3 hours. A shock arrival will probably show first as a sharp jump in solar wind speed and density at the L1 monitor. A sudden impulse at ground magnetometers would follow about 30 to 60 minutes later, depending on the speed of the shock.

sections.heading: Geomagnetic Outlook
sections.text: Storm intensity after arrival depends on the orientation of the magnetic field embedded in the CME, and this cannot be known until the CME reaches L1. If the field turns strongly southward and stays there, G4 (Severe) periods are possible. Storm conditions could last from several hours to about a day after arrival. K-index warnings and alerts will be issued as conditions develop.

sections.heading: Radiation and Radio
sections.text: The greater than 10 MeV proton flux is enhanced but below the S1 (Minor) threshold, and a small chance of S1 continues through 16 Mar. No radio blackout is in progress. HF propagation at high latitudes may be degraded after the CME arrives.

fields.nextIssuance: The next discussion will be issued by 2027 Mar 16 1230 UTC, or sooner if the CME arrives at L1.
fields.footer: *** EXERCISE *** Exercise product. Not an official NOAA discussion. All times UTC.

instructorNote: Main storyline inject. Hand it to both the CRSS and the RCSM. At the same time, read aloud the RC GMD analyst's message on the Notification System: "Our Alert on the G3 watch went out Monday night. Do we send an updated Alert with the CME window? The clock on this discussion started at 0710Z." Watch for two things: (1) the RC issues its updated Alert (the watch Alert went out Monday night) within 15 minutes, with the code, serial, times in UTC and CDT, the 11:00–17:00 CDT window and its uncertainty, a request for Condition 1, the expected duration and the next call, then tracks acknowledgments; (2) the CRSS declares NGDOP Condition 1, logs the code and time, calls the Manager on call, and starts the checks on the GIC monitors, the 14-entity list, the Hartley spare and the outages. The page follows the STARTEX date of 16 March 2027 (CDT, UTC-5), not the November 2026 header date.
